fixes.explanation: Once? Oh no, no, no. God says, "I strongly warned them again and again, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’" (Jeremiah 11:7). That's a whole lot of warnings, and it was never a one-time thing.

False is right. God says, "I strongly warned them again and again, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’" (Jeremiah 11:7). Again and again is a lot more than once, and it covers the time from Egypt until that day.

Not quite, friend. The verse says, "…these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:12). Judah will go and cry out to the gods they have been burning incense to. Those gods certainly will not save them.

False is right. God says, "…these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:12). The very gods they've been burning incense to will not save them. The verse says so plainly.
True. God says, "When you are wicked, then you rejoice." (Jeremiah 11:15). I think it's a sad line. It's what God says about them in that verse.

Roots feel like a natural guess, since the tree was planted. But the verse goes another way: "…with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed." (Jeremiah 11:16). Fire is what the verse says will happen to the tree.

Planted. The verse says, "The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you…" (Jeremiah 11:17). Planted is the exact word the verse uses. He's the one who put them in the ground, so the olive tree picture fits together.
